tier_reason: First-party README slide deck (Apr 2016) gives relative-time tables against Python 3.4.x and Ruby 2.1.x with CPU models named, and the benchmark driver DINO/compare.tst is public, but the compiler version and flags used to build the interpreter are not stated, so not A. The companion paper (dino-lang/implemenation-article, dino.pdf) is the author's own arXiv preprint, not peer-reviewed, so not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: x86-64 (relative times, Dino best = 1.0; plain Dino without hints / Python / Ruby): Loop 19 / 257 / 157; Fact 13.2 / 90.4 / 25.2; Fib 112 / 492 / 142; Method 1.0 / 5.8 / 1.5; Object 1.0 / 4.4 / 1.4; Sieve 1.0 / 37.9 / 4.5; Thread 1.0 / 125 / 43.6; Start 1.0 / 10.9 / 29.4; Hash 1.0 / 2.4 / 2.2. PyPy beats plain Dino on loop (8.1 vs 19), hash (0.4), fact (0.4 vs 13.2), fib (59 vs 112), except (0.4), method (0.2), object (0.1) and random (0.9 vs 3.1), and beats even Dino's best hinted row on hash, fact, except, method, object and random.
corrections.license: GPL-2.0-or-later (DINO interpreter sources; COPYING is GPLv2) and LGPL-2.0-or-later (AMMUNITION library sources; COPYING.LIB is the Library GPL v2)
corrections.caveats: Results are from a 2016 README slide deck (version 0.98 development) on Python 3.4 and Ruby 2.1; numbers are relative to Dino's best run, not seconds. Dino's best row uses JIT, pure-function and inline hints; the plain row is quoted here. PyPy is faster than plain Dino on 8 of 14 benchmarks on x86-64. On AARCH64 Python 2.7.5 was used (Python 3 absent) and Python wins hash (0.5 vs 1.7); on ARM Python beats plain Dino on fact (4.4 vs 18.1) and hash (0.6 vs 1.0); on PPC64 Ruby beats plain Dino on loop (17.6 vs 23.2). The thread benchmark compares Dino green threads with GIL-bound OS threads. The benchmark driver is DINO/compare.tst (shell script, old shootout programs); compiler version and flags for the interpreter build are not stated. The companion arXiv preprint (dino.pdf in dino-lang/implemenation-article, dated 2016/4/5) has a variant table on Python 3.3.x and Ruby 2.0.x with different numbers (e.g. x86-64 loop Python 416, Ruby 237), Fedora Core 21, and GCC 4.9.2 used only for JIT compilation. Author is a GCC maintainer; repo dormant since 2019-11-19.

notes: All quoted x86-64 numbers match the README table; the PyPy statement understated where PyPy wins and is corrected. License tightened from file headers (GPL-2.0-or-later interpreter, LGPL-2.0-or-later AMMUNITION library). Metadata confirmed: 129 stars, not archived, not a fork, last commit 2019-11-19 (abandoned).

tier_reason: First-party docs page (docs/kphp-language/kphp-vs-php/benchmarks.md) gives per-run Zend micro_bench/bench timings against PHP 7.4 with OpCache plus vk.com page and ML-kernel timings, but no CPU model, no compiler version, and the modified Zend scripts are not published; vk.com and ML timings are not reproducible. First-party with partial methodology is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: micro_bench avg 3.297 s on PHP 7.4 vs 0.460 s on KPHP; bench avg 0.659 s vs 0.119 s ('KPHP is found to be 5-7 times faster'); vk.com/feed 10.1 s vs 0.95 s, vk.com/im 1.25 s vs 0.46 s, vk.com/ads 0.73 s vs 0.20 s (PHP 7.2); neural networks with huge matrices ~8 s vs 0.24 s; deep decision trees ~5 s vs 0.14 s; README: 'when your code fits best practices, it runs 3-10 times faster than PHP'. Companion walk-through page (docs/various-topics/walk-through-php-kphp-cpp.md, quicksort of an int array): PHP 7.4 ~2100 ms vs KPHP ~480 ms (~4x); with the array_swap_int_keys built-in and no wrapper call, PHP 7.4 ~1950 ms vs KPHP ~270 ms (~7x); hand-written C++ with g++ -Os ~220 ms.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the Zend runs (PHP 7.4 with OpCache and without XDebug; KPHP version and CPU not given). The walk-through page says KPHP builds its generated C++ with g++ at -Os.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers with no CPU model or KPHP/compiler version. The Zend micro_bench.php and bench.php had a couple of tests removed and errors corrected before running, and the modified scripts are not published. The doc itself calls the Zend comparison 'absolutely synthetic' and warns it is wrong to say KPHP is always faster (code dominated by C-implemented PHP functions such as strpos or parse_url gains almost nothing). The walk-through shows KPHP dropping to ~940 ms when types degrade to mixed[], and hand-written C++ still about 2x faster than plain KPHP. Baseline is PHP 7.4/7.2, without the PHP 8 JIT, so today's gap is probably smaller. vk.com page timings and ML kernels are not reproducible from public code. KPHP only compiles a restricted, strictly typed PHP subset (no generators, anonymous classes, SPL or XML), so existing code usually needs rewriting. The project website is on github.io (blocked here); pages were read from the repo's docs/ directory.

notes: Every quoted number matches the benchmarks.md page; added the walk-through quicksort numbers and the -Os build flag the docs mention. Metadata confirmed: GPL-3.0, about 1.5k stars, not archived, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-25 (active). Tier C stays.
